```md
# `chezmoi init --prompt*` flag silently ignored when prompt text doesn't match

## Symptom

A `docker build` (or `chezmoi init --apply` over SSH / in any TTY-less
environment) fails at the very last step with:

\```
chezmoi: template: chezmoi.toml:23:16: executing "chezmoi.toml" at
<promptChoiceOnce . "profile" "Which profile" $profileChoices $defaultProfile>:
error calling promptChoiceOnce: could not open a new TTY: open /dev/tty:
no such device or address
\```

…even though the build script clearly passes a flag that *looks* like it
should pre-answer the prompt:

\```dockerfile
RUN ~/.local/bin/chezmoi init --apply --source=/tmp/dotfiles-source \
    --promptString "profile (ubuntu_server|ubuntu_desktop|macos|centos_server)=centos_server" \
    ...
\```

The bug is invisible when the value being passed happens to equal the
template's default (e.g. on Linux `$defaultProfile = "ubuntu_server"`
and the build also passes `ubuntu_server`). It fires only when the
override differs from the template default.

## Root cause

`chezmoi init`'s `--promptBool` / `--promptString` / `--promptChoice`
flags **match by the prompt text** (3rd argument to `promptXOnce` in
the template), not by the key name (2nd argument). They are also
**type-strict**: a `--promptString` flag will not satisfy a
`promptChoiceOnce` template call.

In our `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`:

\```
$profile := promptChoiceOnce . "profile" "Which profile" $profileChoices $defaultProfile
\```

The matchable prompt text is **`Which profile`**, and the matching flag
type is **`--promptChoice`**. The pre-fix Dockerfile passed the wrong
flag type AND the wrong text:

\```
--promptString "profile (ubuntu_server|ubuntu_desktop|macos|centos_server)=..."
\```

Two failures stacked:

1. `--promptString` cannot answer a `promptChoiceOnce` call (type
   mismatch). chezmoi silently ignores the unmatched flag.
2. Even if the flag type were `--promptChoice`, the text
   `profile (ubuntu_server|...)` doesn't equal `Which profile` — still
   no match.

When no flag matches, chezmoi falls back to interactive prompting; in a
Docker `RUN` step there is no TTY, so it errors out.

**Why the Ubuntu Dockerfile appeared to work**: chezmoi's
`promptChoiceOnce` returns the template's default value when no
existing config file exists *and* no matching flag is supplied. The
default on Linux happens to be `ubuntu_server`, which also happens to
be the default value of `CHEZMOI_PROFILE` in the existing Dockerfile.
Coincidence kept the bug latent. The first `docker build` that
overrode `CHEZMOI_PROFILE=centos_server` (i.e. our Dockerfile.centos7
/ Dockerfile.rocky9) blew up immediately. The `desktop` compose
service that sets `CHEZMOI_PROFILE=ubuntu_desktop` was almost
certainly broken too — just nobody ran `just docker-desktop` often
enough to notice.

## Fix

Use `--promptChoice` (matching the template's `promptChoiceOnce` call
type) and quote the actual prompt text verbatim:

\```dockerfile
--promptChoice "Which profile=${CHEZMOI_PROFILE}" \
\```

`scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py` was already doing this correctly
(`argv += ["--promptChoice", f"{by_key['profile'].prompt_text}={...}"]`)
because its `Prompt` records carry both `key` and `prompt_text` and it
uses the latter for flag generation. The Dockerfile predates that
wrapper and was never updated when the prompt text in the template
diverged from the key.

## Why `dotfiles_init.py doctor` didn't catch this

The `doctor` subcommand only verifies that **ARG names** in the
`Dockerfile` match the prompt **keys** in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` and
`PROMPTS` in `dotfiles_init.py`. It doesn't parse the actual `--prompt*`
flag text used in the `RUN ~/.local/bin/chezmoi init …` block, so
flag-text drift is invisible to it.

A future enhancement would be: in `doctor_scan`, also regex-extract
`--prompt(String|Bool|Choice)\s+"([^=]+)=` from the Dockerfile's
`chezmoi init` invocation and assert that text matches the template's
prompt text for that key. Tracked in `TODO.md` as `[P2][S] doctor:
verify Dockerfile --prompt* flag text matches template`.

## Related

- `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py` — wrapper that does it right; the
  comment above `_chezmoi_argv` explains the prompt-text rule
  ("Verified empirically against chezmoi 2.68.0 / 2.69.4 / 2.70.2 …").
- `Dockerfile` / `Dockerfile.centos7` / `Dockerfile.rocky9` — the
  three places where `chezmoi init --prompt*` is called from a
  `RUN` step. All three must use prompt-text form, not key-name form.
- `pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md` — sibling pitfall surfaced by the same
  CentOS install-test infrastructure that triggered this debug.
- `CLAUDE.md` → "Dockerfile + dotfiles_init wrapper" invariant —
  documents the parity requirement; this pitfall is the reason
  doctor's text-level check would be a worthwhile extension.

```

```text
#!/bin/sh
# chezmoi modify_ script: maintain ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json (the *global*
# skills-cli lock file at https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills).
#
# Why managed?  The skills CLI does not yet support `npx skills install -g`
# from a lock file (see vercel-labs/skills #283 / #549). So to keep "must-have"
# global agent skills consistent across machines we treat the lock file as the
# single source of truth: this script merges the *managed set* below into
# whatever the live lock contains, then `run_onchange_after_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl`
# reinstalls any entries whose `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` is missing.
#
# Why merge instead of overwrite?  Locally added skills (`npx skills add … -g`
# without `-y` followed by chezmoi re-add) should NOT be wiped on every
# `chezmoi apply`.  We only enforce *presence* of the managed entries; any
# extra `skills.<name>` entries in the live file are preserved verbatim,
# along with `dismissed` flags and `lastSelectedAgents` per-machine state.
#
# To add a new must-have global skill: append an object to $managed.skills below,
# matching the schema chezmoi found when first running `npx skills add … -g`
# (run `cat ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` after a fresh install for reference).
#
# Requires: jq (installed by the `base` ansible role).
# See: docs/tools/agent-skills.md
set -eu

managed=$(cat <<'JSON'
{
  "version": 3,
  "skills": {
    "project-knowledge-harness": {
      "source": "daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills",
      "sourceType": "github",
      "sourceUrl": "https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills.git",
      "skillPath": "skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/SKILL.md"
    },
    "find-skills": {
      "source": "vercel-labs/skills",
      "sourceType": "github",
      "sourceUrl": "https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills.git",
      "skillPath": "skills/find-skills/SKILL.md"
    }
  }
}
JSON
)

base=$(cat)
[ -z "$base" ] && base='{"version":3,"skills":{}}'

# Merge strategy:
#   - .version: take the higher of the two (forward-compatible with skills CLI bumps)
#   - .skills: for every name in $managed.skills, ensure presence; if the live file
#     already has it, keep its installedAt/updatedAt/skillFolderHash (they encode
#     real install state) but overwrite source/sourceUrl/skillPath from $managed
#     (those are the contract we enforce).
#   - .skills.<name> entries NOT in $managed.skills are preserved as-is.
#   - .dismissed and .lastSelectedAgents: preserve from live (per-machine state).
printf '%s' "$base" | jq --argjson managed "$managed" '
  . as $base
  | ($base.skills // {}) as $live_skills
  | ($managed.skills // {}) as $managed_skills
  | {
      version: ([($base.version // 0), ($managed.version // 0)] | max),
      skills: (
        $live_skills
        + (
            $managed_skills
            | to_entries
            | map({
                key: .key,
                value: (
                  ($live_skills[.key] // {})
                  + (.value | with_entries(select(.key | IN("source","sourceType","sourceUrl","skillPath"))))
                )
              })
            | from_entries
          )
      )
    }
    + (if ($base.dismissed // null) != null         then {dismissed:         $base.dismissed}         else {} end)
```

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# Smoke tests intended to run inside the Docker `test` service container
# (see docker-compose.yml). They assert the post-`chezmoi apply` + post-ansible
# state of a fresh Ubuntu box.
#
# Do NOT run these on a host machine — they assume the chezmoi source lives at
# /tmp/dotfiles-source (matches Dockerfile COPY target) and that the container
# has just completed a full install.

load "../test_helper.bash"

SOURCE_DIR="${CHEZMOI_SOURCE_DIR:-/tmp/dotfiles-source}"

@test "chezmoi apply is idempotent (diff is empty after re-apply)" {
  # Re-apply should be a no-op. A non-empty diff means templates drift or
  # run_once state tracking is broken.
  run chezmoi apply
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  run chezmoi diff
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
```

git add Dockerfile Dockerfile.centos7 Dockerfile.rocky9 pitfalls/chezmoi-init-prompt-flag-mismatch.md && git status --short && echo --- && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
docker: install jq + force UTF-8 locale on CentOS 7

Fixes two bugs surfaced by exercising centos7 / rocky9 builds:

1. jq missing during `chezmoi apply` — the modify_ scripts under
   dot_agents/ (and others) shell out to jq during chezmoi's apply
   phase, which runs BEFORE the ansible base role can install jq
   system-wide. Result: `.agents/.skill-lock.json: exit status 127`
   (jq: command not found). Verified: ubuntu:24.04, rockylinux:9 and
   centos:7 all ship without jq, so this is a latent bug in the
   existing Ubuntu Dockerfile too — `just docker-test` would have
   regressed since commit 9eb1fc2 added the modify_ skill-lock script.
   Fix: add jq to the package-install step in all three Dockerfiles
   (apt for ubuntu, yum+epel for centos7, dnf for rocky9).

2. CentOS 7 base image leaves LANG unset → ansible-galaxy fails with
   "Ansible requires the locale encoding to be UTF-8; Detected None."
   The bootstrap's locale-fix branch only triggers on `cannot set`
   errors from `locale`, which a clean centos:7 doesn't emit (LANG is
   simply absent). Fix: install glibc-common and pin LANG/LC_ALL=
   en_US.UTF-8 via ENV in Dockerfile.centos7 so chezmoi/ansible inherit
   a working locale unconditionally.

Also tracks the prior `--promptString "profile (...)"` mismatch as
pitfalls/chezmoi-init-prompt-flag-mismatch.md (committed as part of
this batch since it shares the "exercising centos_server in Docker
finally surfaced latent dotfiles install bugs" theme).

The CentOS 7 sudo flavor still hits a separate Linuxbrew-vs-old-git
issue (CentOS 7 ships git 1.8.x; Homebrew requires 2.7.0+); deferring
that as a bootstrap-script change of larger scope. centos7-noroot
(the realistic corporate scenario per pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md) is
unaffected by the Linuxbrew gate.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-06 14:34:55Z)**_

Rocky9 came incredibly close — bootstrap, jq, ansible-galaxy, all worked. The fatal error is a real role bug: `devtools : Install tmux plugins via TPM` runs even when `tmux` isn't installed (noRoot can't install tmux without sudo on RedHat), so `tmux source-file` fails. Plus a benign ripgrep 404 (no `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` build for ripgrep 15.1.0) that's already gracefully ignored.

CentOS 7 has the locale issue still — `glibc-common` installs but the locale isn't actually *generated* in the stripped centos:7 minimal image. Need explicit `localedef`.

Pragmatic path: set `allowPartialFailure=true` on the noroot services too so the apply finishes past the TPM bug, fix the centos7 locale generation, then file the TPM-needs-tmux gate as a follow-up bug.

Each item carries two tags:

investigation, design notes, or paused troubleshooting — read that first before
re-investigating. Items without a link are simple enough to act on directly.

with a one-line summary of what shipped.

docker: generate en_US.UTF-8 locale on CentOS 7 + allow partial failures on noroot

CentOS 7 fix: the bare `glibc-common` install only ships locale source
data, not the compiled archive — `locale -a | grep en_US.UTF-8`

skill-lock: replace jq IN/1 with as-bound index/1 (jq 1.4+ compatible)

preserves installedAt, managed values overwrite source/sourceUrl,
non-allowlisted keys from managed are stripped).

EOF
)"

Root cause found. `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl:49-50` unconditionally exports `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8` — overriding my Dockerfile's `en_US.UTF-8`. CentOS 7's glibc 2.17 lacks `C.UTF-8` so ansible bails. Fix the script to detect what's available.

<tool-use data-tool-type="shell" data-tool-name="Bash"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Bash**</summary>
Commit ENV PATH + bats gate + locale fallback fixes

```bash
git add Dockerfile Dockerfile.centos7 Dockerfile.rocky9 dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml .chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
docker+centos: ENV PATH for test CMD, broaden bats gate, glibc-2.17 locale fallback

Three small fixes that together let `just docker-test-rocky9` /
`docker-test-centos7` actually run the bats smoke suite end-to-end:

1. Dockerfile{,.centos7,.rocky9}: ENV PATH=/home/devuser/.local/bin:$PATH
   after USER devuser. Docker's CMD doesn't load ~/.bashrc, so the
   test service's `command: ["bats", ...]` exits 127 (executable not
   found) even though the image has bats installed in ~/.local/bin.
   Same hardening applies to the Ubuntu test image.

2. devtools role: broaden the `bats` user-level fallback gate from
   `os_family == "Debian"` to `in ["Debian", "RedHat"]`. The task
   downloads a source tarball from GitHub and runs install.sh — no
   apt-specific behaviour. Mirrors the gate-broadening pattern from
   pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md (already applied to base/starship/
   security_tools/rust_cargo_tools). Without this, RedHat-family
   noRoot installs never get bats and smoke test #6 ("core CLI tools
   on PATH: rg fd jq fzf zsh just bats") fails.

3. .chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl:
   the unconditional `export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8` was clobbering the
   en_US.UTF-8 set by Dockerfile.centos7's ENV. CentOS 7's glibc 2.17
   doesn't ship C.UTF-8 (added properly in glibc 2.35), so every
   ansible role aborted with "Ansible could not initialize the
   preferred locale: unsupported locale setting". Now we probe
   `locale -a`, prefer C.UTF-8 when available, fall back to
   en_US.UTF-8, otherwise leave whatever the parent shell set.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
```

**Final state — 7 commits on `main`, all clean.**

## Summary

### What works
- ✅ **`Dockerfile.centos7`** + **`Dockerfile.rocky9`**: build successfully (centos7 with `allowPartialFailure=true` to absorb deeper Python 3.6 issues; rocky9 cleanly with two known role bugs partially failing)
- ✅ **6 new compose services**: `centos7` / `centos7-noroot` / `rocky9` / `rocky9-noroot` + `test-centos7` / `test-rocky9`, all gated behind `--profile centos|rocky|test`
- ✅ **9 new just recipes**: `docker-build-centos7`, `docker-run-centos7-noroot`, `docker-test-rocky9`, etc.
- ✅ **rocky9-noroot smoke tests**: **5 of 8 passing**, including the just-fixed neovim path. The 3 failures all trace to the same un-broadened-yet devtools roles.

### Bugs surfaced and fixed in-flight (latent in the existing Ubuntu Dockerfile too)
1. `--promptString "profile (...)"` should have been `--promptChoice "Which profile=..."` — would have silently broken `desktop` profile
2. `jq` missing in all 3 base images during `chezmoi apply` (modify_ scripts shell out to it pre-ansible)
3. `IN/1` jq function unused-since-1.6 in `dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl` — broke CentOS 7's EPEL jq 1.5
4. `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8` unconditionally exported in ansible runner — fails on glibc 2.17 (CentOS 7); now probes `locale -a` and falls back to `en_US.UTF-8`
5. `ENV PATH=~/.local/bin:$PATH` missing — Docker `command:` couldn't find tools installed by ansible's user-level path
6. `bats` user-level fallback gated on `os_family == "Debian"` — same pitfall pattern as the original `centos7-noroot.md`
7. `neovim` user-level fallback (and arch fact) gated on `Debian` only — fixed in the same pattern

### Tracked in TODO.md as known-blockers (deliberately deferred)
- **`[L]` devtools role**: ~30 more user-level fallback tasks (rg, fd, bat, gh, eza, delta, etc.) still `Debian`-only — same gate-broadening pattern, mechanical batch fix
- **`[L]` CentOS 7 Python 3.6 vs ansible 2.18 modules**: needs `ANSIBLE_PYTHON_INTERPRETER` pinned to uv-managed 3.13
- **`[M]` CentOS 7 sudo / Linuxbrew vs git 1.8**: bootstrap should skip Linuxbrew when git < 2.7
- **`[S]` ripgrep aarch64 musl 404**: ripgrep 15.1.0+ stopped publishing musl arm64 — fall back to gnu
- **`[S]` devtools TPM-needs-tmux gate**: TPM install fatal when tmux missing
- **`[S]` doctor enhancement**: verify `--prompt*` flag text matches template (would have caught bug #1 above)

### What you can do now
```bash
just docker-build-rocky9        # Build rocky9-noroot + rocky9 (sudo path)
just docker-run-rocky9-noroot   # Interactive shell on rocky9 noroot
just docker-test-rocky9         # 5/8 bats pass; 3 fail due to tracked role gaps
just docker-test-centos7        # Currently blocked on Python 3.6 issue
just docker-clean               # Clean everything
```

The infrastructure is now a measurable scorecard for "% of dotfiles install works on RedHat-family." Each TODO item moves the needle.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-06 15:55:18Z)**_

I see you've added a new `primaryShell` prompt to the Dockerfiles — that's why the test images rebuilt. While the rocky9-noroot image still has the previous build's state (zsh installed), the **rebuilt** test-rocky9 image hit a deeper design issue I hadn't noticed before:

```
chezmoi source-path → /home/devuser/.local/share/chezmoi
ls /home/devuser/.local/share/chezmoi → No such file or directory
```

**The bats test calls bare `chezmoi apply`** (test 1), but our 3 Dockerfiles only set up the source via `--source=/tmp/dotfiles-source` for the *initial* init — chezmoi's persistent source-dir defaults to `~/.local/share/chezmoi/` which is empty. Bare `chezmoi apply` therefore exits 1, cascading test 1 → test 2 → 3 → 8 to all fail.

This was always a latent bug — the existing Ubuntu Dockerfile has the exact same issue. The earlier "5/8 passing" run on rocky9 must have used a cached image from a coincidentally-working state. The two background tasks (centos7 test + rocky9 sudo build) are still running; will report when they finish, then we can decide on the source-dir fix together — likely either symlink `~/.local/share/chezmoi` → `/tmp/dotfiles-source` in all 3 Dockerfiles, or change the bats test to use `--source=$SOURCE_DIR`.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-06 15:56:07Z)**_

centos7 test failed at container start: `bats: not found` — because all 9 ansible tags failed (Python 3.6 vs ansible 2.18 modules) so bats was never installed. Same root cause already filed in TODO.md (`ANSIBLE_PYTHON_INTERPRETER` pin to uv's Python 3.13).

The `docker-build-rocky9` is still mid-stream (currently downloading mise — sudo path runs Linuxbrew + dnf installs so takes longer). Will report when it finishes.

**Current results so far**

| Recipe | Result | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `docker-test-rocky9` | 3 ok / 5 not ok | The `chezmoi source-path` mismatch breaks tests 1, 2, 3, 6, 8 — bare `chezmoi apply` looks at `~/.local/share/chezmoi` (empty) instead of `/tmp/dotfiles-source` |
| `docker-test-centos7` | container can't start | bats absent (Python 3.6 issue blocks every ansible role; even with `allowPartialFailure=true` no tools get installed) |
| `docker-build-rocky9` | running | Sudo path — Linuxbrew + dnf packages |

**One realisation worth surfacing now**: the `chezmoi source-path` mismatch is a **pre-existing flaw** in the entire docker-test design (Ubuntu Dockerfile has it too) — `chezmoi init --source=/tmp/dotfiles-source` doesn't persist that path, so any later bare `chezmoi apply` from inside the container fails. The earlier "5/8 passing" run on rocky9 must have benefited from coincidental buildkit cache state.

Two reasonable fixes once the build finishes:
1. **Symlink** `~/.local/share/chezmoi` → `/tmp/dotfiles-source` in all 3 Dockerfiles after `chezmoi init` (preserves the test as-written)
2. **Edit the bats test** to use `chezmoi apply --source="$SOURCE_DIR"` (more explicit; touches every chezmoi invocation)

I'd lean (1) — single-line per Dockerfile, no test churn. Want me to apply that fix once the rocky9 sudo build finishes, or would you prefer to call it a day and let the existing ~7 commits land as-is with TODO entries for both source-dir + Python 3.6 + remaining devtools broadening?
